Description: Foldseek global TMalign of query vs references, then verify that the query backbone is helical at the four mapped core-helix positions
Rationale for selection/rejection: Low recall (0.59): reference-frame-free helix test accepts helicity anywhere the alignment maps, producing false positives; simultaneously misses structures where the global alignment maps poorly despite intact helices

Description: Foldseek reference-normalised TM-score (tTMscore), best of 9 references
Rationale for selection/rejection: High recall but 37 false positives: coarse structural similarity does not distinguish intact from degraded helix bundles

Description: PyMOL super (sequence-independent, structure-based dynamic programming) vs 9 references, best coverage and RMSD
Rationale for selection/rejection: High precision (0.96) but low recall (0.67): stricter convergence criteria than cealign cause the alignment to fail on highly divergent structures in the non-canonical pool

Description: PyMOL cealign (sequence-independent) vs 9 references, best coverage and RMSD
Rationale for selection/rejection: Highest accuracy (85.9%) and F1 (0.90), but 29 false positives: half-bundles with only two helices can achieve high coverage against short references

Description: Reference-free secondary structure assignment (Biotite): count long helices (>= 8 residues) and test for compact four-helix bundle geometry
Rationale for selection/rejection: Near-perfect recall but lowest precision (0.78): any four-helix bundle scores positive regardless of PPO identity, capturing unrelated folds

Description: Combined: M5 intrinsic bundle test AND PPO-identity gate (M1 or M2 positive)
Rationale for selection/rejection: Identity gate reduces M5 false positives but 38 remain; the loose M2 gate still passes degraded structures

Description: Copper-anchored Kabsch + ICP superposition onto the 5 Cu-bearing references, then backbone helicity check at each core-helix position anchored to the copper site
Threshold: 4/4 helices helical, close to ref, and confident
Rationale for selection/rejection: Highest accuracy (90.5%) and perfect precision (1.00, zero false positives). Threshold sensitivity sweep across 400 combinations confirmed FP=0 throughout; widened Cα distance windows (d3: 4.0-6.4 Å, d4: 4.8-8.2 Å) capture 3₁₀ turns and slightly distorted helices without admitting any false positives. Selected because false positives (junk in the non-canonical pool) are more damaging to downstream biological analysis than false negatives (valid structures in the discard pool)
